Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC puzzle solving

Use this procedure when handling an instance in the Continual-ARC stream.

1. Read the task id, test grid, attempt/demo counts, and any received demonstrations. Keep each instance self-contained; do not assume another instance's conversation is available.

5. After the verdict, save the program that reproduced all available pairs to `programs/<task id>.py`, replacing an older version as needed, then issue `finish` once the instance is over.
6. On every response, end with exactly one required action JSON object on the last line: `submit` with a grid, `request_demos`, or `finish`. Respect the attempt cap; each wrong submission and demo request has a cost.

from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    # Background is 7; retain the two large object colors and replace stray colors.
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    keep = {7}
    keep.update(color for color, _ in counts.most_common() if color != 7 and len(keep) < 3)
    return [[value if value in keep else 7 for value in row] for row in grid]
